rows.behavior: Intake: per-source auth (basic, form key, HMAC), 413/415/401/404/429/503 answers, per-IP and per-source rate limits, right-most trusted proxy hop, CORS per source, access log and proxy headers off

claims.claim: Basic auth password stored as an argon2id hash
Form key is random, stored as a SHA-256 hash, names the source; protected by honeypot, rate limits and spam check
The api runs with its access log off, so the key never reaches a log
HMAC over timestamp and body in Firstcall-Timestamp / Firstcall-Signature; more than 5 minutes off is refused; secret in a named env var
Honeypot filled means spam
202 stored, 200 repeat
401 bad credentials, 404 unknown source
413 over 10 MB email / 1 MB form or call, checked while the body streams
415 wrong content type, message/rfc822 for email, application/json otherwise
429: 30 per minute per client address before anything else; 60 per minute per source after auth
503 when the database write fails
IPv6 client counted by its /64
X-Forwarded-For only with FIRSTCALL_TRUST_PROXY; client is the entry FIRSTCALL_TRUSTED_HOPS from the right, default 1
Allowed origins get Access-Control-Allow-Origin; others get none
Email source takes basic auth with user inbox and message/rfc822 on port 8020
The form key is public; sources that must refuse strangers use basic auth or a signature
rotate-secret prints a new key; origin must be in allowed_origins; honeypot name equals honeypot_field

rows.behavior: Duplicate deliveries: Message-ID key (hashed when long or unprintable), raw hash when no Message-ID or headers over budget, delivery-id header, same body within 10 minutes

claims.claim: A Message-ID over 200 characters or with unprintable characters is replaced by its SHA-256
No Message-ID, or headers over the read budget: key is the SHA-256 of the raw message
Form and call: delivery id header, else body hash within 10 minutes

rows.behavior: Read budget and email parsing: text, line and line-length caps; header total and per-parsed-header cap; part and depth limits; recursion caught; default policy with a budget hook; HTML block tags become line breaks; forwards followed to inner sender and Reply-To

claims.claim: Over any limit the message ends failed with the limit in its reason; nothing is cut
200,000 characters, 4,000 lines, 4,000 characters per line
64,000 characters of headers; listed parsed headers capped at 4,000 each; others count only toward the total
At most 100 parts including the message; at most 10 levels with the message first
Stack-overflowing nesting in email or JSON refused the same way
Default policy with a hook that checks each header before it is parsed
Default policy picks the plain or HTML body
Policy hook checks every header of every part before parsing; part factory counts parts
Intake runs a raw-byte header check and a headers-only compat32 parse only for the Message-ID

rows.behavior: Matching: a named message never joins a nameless lead on phone alone; hard negatives never merge; doubtful cases flagged

claims.claim: Compatible-name rule amended to one direction

ADR-003 result recorded and rule amended
